summary: IMF Article IV reports (8 vintages, 2016-2026) give a consistent-looking but heavily revised series of CBI fiscal revenue (FY2012/13-FY2025/26) and BoP CBI inflows (2019-2025): CBI revenue rose from about 2-5% of GDP before 2016 to 30-37% of GDP in FY2020/21-FY2024/25. Budget addresses provide budget targets and a few preliminary outturns that differ from IMF figures, and early IMF vintages under-estimated CBI revenue by factors of 2-3. No official data on applications, approvals or passports issued exist publicly (the IMF says it has no access); only OCCRP analysis and a PM claim are available.

events.title: Citizenship by Investment programme established
events.description: Dominica’s programme (originally the Economic Citizenship Programme) dates from 1993.
events.quote: The Commonwealth of Dominica has had a Citizenship by Investment (CBI) Programme since 1993

events.title: Citizenship by Investment Regulations 2014 gazetted
events.description: S.R.O. 37 of 2014 replaced the 2013 regulations and set fees from 1 January 2014: US$100,000 fund contribution (single applicant) and US$200,000 minimum real-estate investment.

events.title: Real estate option introduced in practice
events.description: IMF reports that in 2015 the government added a real-estate investment option to the programme.
events.quote: In 2015 the government revised the ECP by introducing a new real estate option that grants citizenship in exchange for making investments in Dominica.

events.title: Tropical Storm Erika
events.description: Storm caused damage estimated by the IMF at 96 percent of GDP; CBI resources were used for post-Erika rehabilitation.
events.quote: While Erika had caused severe damage, estimated at 96 percent of GDP

events.title: Temporary cut in real-estate government fees
events.description: S.R.O. 23 of 2017 lowered the government fee on real-estate applications to US$25,000 for a main applicant for 12 months from 1 September 2017.
events.quote: Commencing on the 1st day of September 2017, for a period of 12 months

events.title: Hurricane Maria
events.description: Category 5 hurricane; damage estimated at US$1.3 billion (226 percent of GDP). CBI deposits and revenue financed much of the reconstruction.
events.quote: On September 18, 2017, category 5 Hurricane Maria hit Dominica

events.title: CBI-funded post-Maria housing programme
events.description: The 2018/19 budget address said 3,853 new homes were contracted and that the government had used CBI funds exclusively to reach every community.
events.quote: A total of three thousand, eight hundred and fifty-three (3,853) new homes are already contracted to be built.

events.title: UK imposes visa requirement on Dominica nationals
events.description: The UK Home Secretary cited abuse of Dominica’s CBI scheme, including citizenship granted to people posing a risk to the UK; transition period until 16 August 2023.
events.quote: Careful consideration of Dominica’s and Vanuatu’s operation of a citizenship by investment scheme has shown clear and evident abuse of the scheme

events.title: US$5,000 levy per CBI investor in private developments
events.description: Levy announced in the 2023/24 budget to capitalise the Debt Repayment Fund.
events.quote: This levy will take effect from September 1, 2023

events.title: OCCRP investigation: budget figures imply thousands of undisclosed citizenships
events.description: OCCRP compared gazettes (about 7,700 names, 2007-2022) with naturalisation fees in budgets (enough for more than 19,000 citizens, mid-2016 to mid-2022).
events.quote: More than 10,000 names appear to be undisclosed.

events.title: New Citizenship by Investment Regulations 2024 (S.R.O. 1 of 2024)
events.description: Consolidated regulations; fund contribution still US$100,000 for a main applicant.

events.title: Regional Memorandum of Agreement on CBI published
events.description: Five Eastern Caribbean CBI states agree common standards, information sharing and a regional regulator.
events.quote: The MOA which was published in March 2024 aims to ensure mutual cooperation, information sharing and adherence to common standards of best practice, and regulatory oversight.

events.title: Fund contribution doubled to US$200,000 (S.R.O. 8 of 2024)
events.description: New regulations raise the direct contribution for a main applicant from US$100,000 to US$200,000 and the real-estate government fee to US$75,000.

events.title: Regional US$200,000 minimum price takes effect
events.description: All MOA signatories apply a US$200,000 minimum for any CBI option; discounting declared illegal.
events.quote: With effect from July 01, 2024, all countries have agreed that the minimum price for any CBI options shall be US$200,000.

events.title: Parliament passes Eastern Caribbean CBI Regulatory Authority Act
events.description: Dominica’s parliament passed the ECCIRA Act (regional regulator), per the 2026/27 budget address.
events.quote: The Eastern Caribbean Citizenship by Investment Regulatory Authority Act, passed by Parliament last October

events.title: EU revises visa suspension mechanism to cover investor citizenship schemes
events.description: Regulation (EU) 2025/2441 makes the operation of an investor citizenship scheme a ground for suspending visa-free travel to the EU.
events.quote: the operation, by a third country listed in Annex II, of an investor citizenship scheme

events.title: US partially suspends entry of Dominica nationals from 1 January 2026
events.description: Presidential proclamation includes Dominica and Antigua and Barbuda explicitly because of their CBI programmes.
events.quote: the December one includes countries (i.e., Antigua and Barbuda and Dominica) on the basis of their offering citizenship by investment programs

events.title: European Commission asks CBI states to phase out programmes by 1 June 2028
events.description: Letter from Commissioner Magnus Brunner (reported via the Antigua and Barbuda PM’s office) requests phase-out with a 24-month transition; the five states rejected the demand.
events.quote: The five Eastern Caribbean states with active Citizenship by Investment (CBI) Programmes, have been given until June 1, 2028 to phase out their programmes.

programs.name: Commonwealth of Dominica Citizenship by Investment Programme
programs.notes: Originally the Economic Citizenship Programme (ECP); administered by the Citizenship by Investment Unit (CBIU). Routes: Economic Diversification Fund contribution and approved real estate. Under EU request (June 2026) to phase out by 1 June 2028.

gaps: No official counts of applications received/approved/rejected or persons naturalised; IMF 2026 (PDF p. 66) says details incl. number of passports issued are not available to staff. CBIU publishes none.
Audited public accounts / Director of Audit reports and printed budget estimates (with CBI line items) were not found online; budget addresses were used instead.
Real-estate route inflows (money paid to developers) are not published; IMF BoP 'CBI' line and fiscal line differ in basis and neither clearly covers real estate.
IMF 2019/2020 Article IV staff reports (if any) were not located; FY2012/13-FY2015/16 figures rely on the 2016-2018 reports. Pre-2012 series not found (except WP/15/93 for 2013).
Citizenship by Investment Regulations 2013 (S.R.O. 43 of 2013) and 2023 regulations, and the schedule applying between Sept 2018 and Jan 2024, were not reviewed.
ECCB statistical releases on CBI were not checked; the ECCB relies on cash-based fiscal CBI data (IMF 2026).
OECD 2018 list of potentially high-risk CBI/RBI schemes (Dominica listed per secondary sources) could not be retrieved (oecd.org returned 403/no match).
The European Commission letter of 25 June 2026 is not public; only media reports.
The US proclamation text (whitehouse.gov) was not downloadable; CRS summary used.
